# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

(Environment/system text above is not part of the books; ignore for book Q&A.)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "Won at Last; or, Mrs. Briscoe's Nephews" by Agnes Giberne (Gutenberg #71133)

Publisher: John F. Shaw & Co., London. Chapters I–XXVIII.

### Main characters
- **Marion Hazel** ("I", narrator), wife of Robert; ~18 when married, now ~40s; fair, slight, impulsive. Aunt Briscoe's niece by marriage.
- **Robert Hazel**, husband; London clerk at Peterson & Co., mercantile house; quiet, kind, careworn, "a man of few words", fond of books; father old Mr. Hazel was a midland farmer. Brother of Churton.
- **Churton Hazel**, Robert's younger brother; went to Canada in youth; selfish, loud, bearded later; "always meaning to do right, always doing wrong" (Aunt Briscoe). Called Maimie "my little dove." Later in States, then farming in South Africa.
- **Mrs. Elizabeth Briscoe ("Aunt Briscoe")**, widow of Mr. Briscoe; lives at "The Gables" near London; sharp-tongued, rheumatic gout; Thursday letters; signs "ELIZABETH BRISCOE." Husband (Uncle Briscoe) had gardening passion. Their only child died.
- **Cherry (Cherry Hazel)**, twin of Cress; nearly 16 at start; plump, short, smooth hair, neat; sensible, devout, "my God shall supply all your need" (Phil. 4:19).
- **Cresswell "Cress" Hazel**, twin; handsome, clever-thought, selfish, spoiled, wants college/barrister; thin, pale, curly light hair, blue eyes like Marion. Later clerk; sent to India (with employers); back later; best man at Jack's wedding.
- **Jack (John) Hazel**, eldest (~19 at Bushey Park); tall, broad-shouldered, warm, kind, slow at figures/spelling, honest grey eyes; devoted to Maimie; later his wife. Employers at Peterson's; later Mr. Morison (his office head).
- **Owen Hazel**, ~14 at start; steady, slow-moving, helpful; later office in north of England.
- **Frederick "Fred"**, 10 at start (the three younger boys: Frederick, Robert ("Bob"), Edmund "Ted"/"Teddy", ages 10–7; Ted fair-haired, Ted's favourite seat by mother). Fred later on training-ship for Merchant Navy.
- Six boys total + Cherry + Maimie etc. (family of nine originally).
- **Mary "Maimie" Browne**, stepdaughter of Churton; ~14 at arrival ("nearly fifteen"), turned 17 at Bushey Park birthday (June); flaxen curling hair, black eyes, pale, delicate; quick, wilful, later humble and devout; calls Marion "Aunt Marion," Robert "Uncle Robert." Mother (Mrs. Browne) died, long illness; Maimie read Bible; "dear dear Aunt Marion"; prayer, Saviour.
- **Maria** — Aunt Briscoe's housemaid, sent away; **cook** dislikes Churton.
- **Mr. Wilson** — the lawyer (old grey-haired, Mrs. Briscoe's friend).
- **Mr. Bowen** — passenger who saw Maimie to London cab.
- **Dr.** — parish doctor, elderly, poor.

### Places
Marion's home in London (basement dining room, one gas burner); The Gables (cosy house, drawing-room, conservatory, lawn, garden); Canada, the States; Bushey Park/Hampton Court (excursion by river from London, row up river); Westminster Abbey, St Paul's, Blackfriars.

### Events in order
1. Ch I: Cherry asks for Cress's outdoor shoes; money tight; six growing boys; Robert clerk; Jack slow; Cress wants college. Cherry offers to not get new jacket.
2. Ch II: Postman letter from Aunt Briscoe (invites Robert to visit; Jack first if good boy; "Robert travels third-class"). Maimie Browne arrives claiming to be cousin, daughter of Mrs. Browne who married Churton.
3. Ch III: Robert/Marion question her; Maimie says father in States/Canada; no address; she has one trunk; Jack pays cabman; Maimie sleeps with Cherry.
4. Ch IV: Packet of letters (Churton's letters). Marion: "cannot afford"; Robert: "what if our Master gives it to us to be carried?" Marion says "The girl is an impostor"? no—Marion's hard words "Stepfather tricked you"; Maimie: "I shall never never love you." Maimie decides to stay.
5. Ch V: Saturday visit to Aunt Briscoe (Marion & Robert): she says "The Parish," i.e. workhouse suggestion; refuses money ("never give where I'm asked").
6. Ch VI: Cherry & Marion talk about trust; Phil 4:19 "All your need"; "cast your care".
7. Ch VII: Boys late from Westminster/St Paul's trip; Owen explains; Maimie's wilfulness; Marion warns Maimie. Postman watching.
8. Ch VIII: Maimie does housework; Jack's jealousy; Maimie drooping, side-ache.
9. Ch IX: Maimie collapses (inflammation, appendicitis-like). Marion's jealousy and impatience.
10. Ch X: Robert home; Maimie upstairs; night; Maimie asks to go to hospital; Marion holds her, "I do love you"; Jack cries; decision to keep her.
11. Ch XI: Long illness; Parish doctor; gifts from Jack's employers; Aunt Briscoe sends £5. Maimie asks Jack about his 'mistakes'; Jack's employer warns him.
12. Ch XII: Maimie advises Jack: "bad habit… you can get over it"; offers to teach Jack figures and Bob/Ted lessons.
13. Ch XIII: Aunt Briscoe visits; takes Maimie to The Gables for a week (becomes four weeks).
14. Ch XIV: Cress's offer: Cress placed in mercantile house; Churton's letter with £25 bank note (America); Maimie: "Aunt Briscoe very kind"; Aunt Briscoe's offer rejected.
15. Ch XV: Two years pass; Jack 19, Cress 18, Owen in north, Fred on training ship. Hampton Court excursion for Maimie's 17th birthday (June); Robert & Marion sit in Bushey Park; Marion frets about Jack and Cress rivalry.
16. Ch XVI: Jack alone in Bushey Park, sobbing ("no hope of Maimie"); Maimie tells Marion that Cress proposed; Maimie rejected both; Marion: "I love Aunt Marion."; back home Churton appears in sitting-room (stout, black beard, loud voice).
17. Ch XVII: Churton's arrival; he insults Maimie; Maimie defends Robert/Marion; Churton hints he'll claim Maimie; Marion suspects Churton plots against Aunt Briscoe's money.
18. Ch XVIII: Churton stays nearby; Cress jealous of Jack; Jack confides to Marion, "Maimie is my idol." Marion warns him: "Then either your idol will separate you..."
19. Ch XIX: Ted (then Bob, Cherry, Maimie) get measles; Maimie catches; inflammation; Churton refuses to visit; Maimie: "I brought all this on myself"; she recovers after ~10 weeks.
20. Ch XX: Churton sends £20 cheque; Maimie's fight with Cress (Cress hits Jack, then Maimie's arm bruised); Maimie says she likes Jack best.
21. Ch XXI: Cress to India (his wish to leave); Cress asks Marion; Robert consults employers. Aunt Briscoe refuses visits; Churton "staying at The Gables."
22. Ch XXII: Cress sails early Feb; Jack gives Marion new Bible. Robert and Jack refused at The Gables; Maimie writes letter to father; Maimie learns of will (Robert's expectation); decides to confront Churton.
23. Ch XXIII: Maimie's letter ("I MUST"); Churton comes to Marion's house; Maimie asks "do I belong to you or Uncle Robert?"; Churton demands she come with him; Maimie threatens; Churton says he'll take her "this afternoon."
24. Ch XXIV: Maimie leaves for The Gables with Churton; "It is for Uncle's sake."
25. Ch XXV: Robert visits The Gables; sees Maimie; Maimie gives a private note.
26. Ch XXVI: Maimie's note ("Aunt Briscoe was offended"; Churton withholding letters); Aunt Briscoe dies of paralytic stroke; Churton's telegram; funeral.
27. Ch XXVII: Will read by Mr. Wilson: first will (Robert gets The Gables, ~£700/yr); codicil 3 months before death leaves all to Churton, £500 to Robert; later codicil (less than 3 weeks before death) reverts all to Robert + £1000 to Jack. Churton furious; "Girl, this is your doing?"; disowns Maimie; leaves.
28. Ch XXVIII: Maimie explains she reconciled Aunt Briscoe to Robert, Aunt Briscoe found Christ-ish ("Just as I am"); family moves to The Gables; Jack proposes to Maimie in garden ("My own"); three years later wedding; Churton letter from South Africa with £5 gift; "Since then we have heard no more of Churton."

Note: Maimie was called "Mary"; Aunt Briscoe said "Mary Browne."

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Out of the Blue" by Bertrand W. Sinclair (Gutenberg #73542; orig. Blue Book Magazine, July 7, 1927)

Chapters I–XVI (titled chapters, e.g. "CHAPTER I: A RETAINING FEE").

### Main characters
- **Rock (Rock) Holloway**, narrator-protagonist; young Texan cowpuncher, long-limbed, tall-ish (a bit over medium height), deeply tanned, gray Stetson, buckskin gloves; rides bright sorrel horse **Sangre** (also black pony with white star later? — Sangre sorrel with white star on forehead; black pony for bed; chunky bay for work). Father Steve Holloway (ex-US marshal at Abilene); uncle Tom Holloway, "Long Tom," Texas ranger; cousin Ben Holloway (Ragged H on Milk River). Sister Cecilia "Cissy" (to marry a Brett, B X near El Paso, fall). Mother in Austin. Educated in East (Eastern schooling). Had $2000 savings plans.
- **Uncle Bill Sayre** — "Uncle Bill," president/manager of Trinity Bank, Fort Worth, Texas; ~60, tall thin face; speaks with Southern dialect ("yo'"); executor of Dave Snell's will; hires Rock: $500 advance in gold, $60/month.
- **Dave Snell** — deceased cattle owner, Maltese Cross brand, Trinity River; had ~30,000 cattle; moved to Montana (Marias River); estate to two children: **Alice Snell** (girl, 21, blonde/tawny hair, blue/pansy-blue eyes, black eyebrows, beautiful; wears green corduroy split skirt; loves Doc) and boy (16, executes later). Estate to run till boy 25.
- **Buck Walters** — coadministrator/range boss of Maltese Cross; young, ambitious, high-handed, flashy dresser, fond of women & poker; big, silver-banded high-crowned hat; black horse with white face; cool, cold eyes; killed by Rock on East Butte (shot through chest by Rock's carbine).
- **Dave Wells** — Texan boss of the Steering Wheel (Wagon Wheel?) on Old Man River north of Canada; tall, thin, drawly; Buck's friend; later killed in battle (Rock: "Wells fought 'em to the last").
- **Mark Duffy** — big bully, 6+ ft, of Seventy Seven trail herd; killed by Rock at Clark's Ford's Odeon, Nebraska.
- **Elmer Duffy** — Mark's brother, trail boss of Seventy Seven; slaty eyes; homely, angular face; wants Nona; later friendly after Rock.
- **Joe Duffy** (Joe, noisy), **Ed** (tough), **Mark** (dead). Four Duffy boys.
- **Al Kerr** — little Texan cowman, ~5'4", gnomelike, Capital K outfit in Judith Basin (Arrow Creek; Lewistown post office, Buffalo Creek). Rock helps him earlier; later helps Rock with 12–50 men.
- **Nona Parke** — owner of TL ranch on Marias River; ~21 (18 at arrival 4 years earlier; "had just finished school"); dark hair, gray eyes "like pools," scarlet lips, slender, dominant, independent; father (Parke) died after horse fell on him; mother died when Betty born; came with 9,000 cattle, lost most in winter; ~800 cattle now. Dislikes men who get "sentimental." Kissed by Rock.
- **Betty Parke** — 3-year-old (fair-haired, blue-eyed, round face, rag doll), called Rock "Doc."
- **Doc Martin** — former TL rider, twin-like double of Rock (same build, age, features); killed by bushwhack ambush, shot in saddle, a week before Rock's arrival; buried by Rock & Nona near parents on Marias ("Doc Martin dead, buried beside dad and mamma"). Loved Nona/Alice; quarrelled with Elmer Duffy. Doc's saddle bloodstained (yellow leather).
- **Charlie Shaw** — 20ish boy, blond, blue eyes, Parke rider with TL/Parke brand; loyal to Nona; later shot at East Butte (survived, sent to Benton).
- **Mary Vieux** — half-breed girl ~16, moon-faced, nurse/cook to Betty; "Mary."
- **Joe Stack** — ambushing gunman (Texan; killed/ hair-macarte tied, burned foot); with **Bill Hurley** (who shot Doc). Paid $500 total by Buck; Stack paid; Hurley killed.
- **Burris boys** — Goosebill rustlers (behind the Goosebill hill) framed as Doc's partners.

### Places
Fort Worth TX (Trinity Bank, Trinity River); Clark's Ford, Nebraska (Odeon dance hall; Platte-like river, ferry/ford; Ben Clark named it); Wyoming; Yellowstone; Fort MacLeod, Canada (Steering Wheel winter); Sweet Grass Hills; Milk River; Fort Assiniboine; Marias River valley; Fort Benton (Grand Union Hotel; ferry; Missouri); Goosebill hill; Bear Paws; Sweet Grass Hills (Gold Butte, West Butte, East Butte — hidden corrals on East Butte); White Springs (Maltese Cross round-up); Billings (N.P. Hotel; telegraph); Judith Basin (Capital K, Arrow Creek); Lonesome Prairie; Seventy Seven ranch on Marias (~upper); Lewistown.

### Key events in order
1. Ch I (Fort Worth, April): Rock gets $500 gold advance (retainer) from Uncle Bill to watch Maltese Cross range manager Buck Walters in Montana (Marias River, Fort Benton post office). Rock's wages $60/mo; Uncle Bill suspicious of Buck (Snell estate). Rock rides north with Seventy Seven herd (Elmer Duffy, boss).
2. Ch II (July, Clark's Ford): In Odeon, Mark Duffy bullies Al Kerr, fires shot; Rock shoots Mark dead. Kerr's riders help; Rock leaves Seventy Seven.
3. Ch III: Rock rides north; joins a short-handed trail herd (Maltese Cross brand/ Steering Wheel?) to Canada; winters with Dave Wells's Steering Wheel outfit at Old Man River (Canada, Fort MacLeod); sees suspicious doggies (freshly branded Steering Wheel over Texan cattle). Leaves in spring (June).
4. Ch IV (Marias, June): Rock hires as packer for US cavalry (Fort Assiniboine); arrives Marias valley; finds Doc Martin's body in ranch house; Nona and Betty; resemblance; buries Doc.
5. Ch V–VI: Burial at dawn; Nona offers job; Rock accepts (Doc's job). Meets Elmer Duffy; claims identity as Doc Martin to avoid feud.
6. Ch VII: Rides to Maltese Cross round-up at White Springs; meets Alice Snell, Charlie Shaw, Buck Walters (who stares, hostile). Learns Maltese Cross/rustling gossip.
7. Ch VIII: Charlie Shaw reveals Doc's identity; Burris rumours; Rock reveals to Charlie he is not Doc (Charlie loyal).
8. Ch IX: Fort Benton; meets Buck and Dave Wells at bar; Rock identifies himself as Rock Holloway to Wells; Buck says "This country ain't healthy for you... South"; threatens Rock: "inside of forty-eight hours."
9. Ch X: Alice Snell warns Rock; vigilance committee (Buck, Elmer Duffy, Seventy Seven & Maltese Cross riders, Charlie among them) comes to hang "Doc" for rustling; Rock covers the porch; Nona denies Rock's guilt; Buck claims Doc was in with Burrises; Elmer accepts; Alice denounces Buck ("I hate you") and Buck leaves.
10. Ch XI: Rock & Nona talk; Rock kisses? (no—kiss is Ch XIII); Charlie, Nona; Rock rides to gather horses with Charlie, ambushed in ravine; Rock shoots two men (Joe Stack & Bill Hurley; Hurley's sorrel dropped; Stack captured, hog-tied).
11. Ch XII: Rock interrogates Stack (burns foot); Stack confesses Buck offered $500 to kill Rock; Hurley shot Doc Martin; Buck to go North with hand-picked crew; Rock releases Stack on Maltese Cross horse.
12. Ch XIII: Nona dresses Rock's head wound (slash on scalp, court-plaster); Rock says he'll go "on the warpath"; Rock kisses Nona before leaving; Rock rides to Fort Benton, ferry; heads to Judith Basin (Kerr) and Billings; telegram from Uncle Bill: "Act on your own judgment. Will back any action you take. Suspected this. Coming north, first train. Sayre."
13. Ch XIV: Billings telegram; Rock returns with Kerr's men (12–14 riders, wagon); Charlie Shaw meets them: Buck and six pets camped on creek near corrals; 5 more riders with pack outfit arrived.
14. Ch XV: Sweet Grass Hills, East Butte; hidden corrals (dumbbell shape, branding chute); Buck, Wells rebranding Maltese Cross to Steering Wheel; Charlie shot by lookout (fell into wild cherry); Rock's horse shot; chase; Rock shoots Buck (at 20 yards) as Buck charges; Buck's black white-faced horse killed by Rock; Kerr men arrive; Wells died fighting.
15. Ch XVI: Rock at Maltese Cross house with Uncle Bill; Maltese Cross brand worked on ~2000 head; Sayre offers Rock management of Maltese Cross; Rock returns to TL; Elmer Duffy shakes hands with Rock; Charlie wounded, sent to Benton; Rock and Nona: "I like you a heap"; Nona: "I'm certainly not sad!"

Note: Blue Book transcription note: story appeared in July 7, 1927 issue.
